source_read: PMC HTML (PMC5109734; Syst Rev 2016;5:189), saved plain text of the PMC article page read start to end: abstract, Background, Methods (data sources, eligibility, extraction, risk of bias and GRADE, synthesis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses), Results (description of studies with Table 1, risk of bias, abstinence and retention meta-analyses with subgroup analyses, safety, sensitivity analyses, publication bias), Discussion with Table 2 (GRADE evidence profile) and Table 3 (summary of findings), strengths and limitations, conclusions, funding, competing interests, additional-file list and reference list. Figures 1-6 (PRISMA flow, risk-of-bias graphs, forest plots, funnel plots) are images absent from the text (legends only), so trial-level forest-plot data and per-trial risk-of-bias judgments could not be read; Additional files 1-3 not available.

claims.overstatement: Slight: 'with no difference between the two drugs' rests on a non-significant test for subgroup differences (chi-square 0.29, df 1, p = 0.59) between three bupropion and two modafinil trials with wide intervals (modafinil OR 0.86, 0.46-1.61; bupropion 1.12, 0.54-2.33); 'neither drug differed from placebo, and the two did not differ detectably from each other' would match the source more exactly. Otherwise the wording is faithful and non-causal.
claims.note: Numbers recomputed. 70/353 = 19.8% and 62/289 = 21.5% (Table 2); 353 + 289 = 642. OR 0.97 (0.65-1.45), I2 2% (chi-square 4.08, df 4, p = 0.40), p = 0.87. Per 1,000: applying the pooled OR to the pooled placebo risk (62/289 = 215 per 1,000) gives -5.1 (-63.8 to +69.2), i.e. 5 fewer (64 fewer to 69 more), as printed in Tables 2 and 3. Retention: 332/626 = 53.0%, 268/558 = 48.0%; 626 + 558 = 1184; OR 1.20 (0.91-1.58), I2 15% (chi-square 15.34, df 13, p = 0.29); GRADE-style +45.5 (-23.5 to +113.2) per 1,000, printed as 46 more (23 fewer to 113 more). All match. Caution for the editor: '5 fewer per 1,000' is GRADE's model-based absolute effect, not the crude difference between the two percentages the claim also prints (19.8% - 21.5% = 1.6 points, 16 fewer per 1,000; crude OR 0.91); a reader setting the two side by side may see a mismatch. Same for retention (crude +50 per 1,000 vs GRADE +46). Not an error in the claim, but if both are shown the per-1,000 figure should be labelled as the summary-of-findings estimate. Other points the claim does not carry: (a) both outcomes are rated very low certainty by the authors (abstinence: risk of bias very serious, inconsistency serious, indirectness serious, imprecision very serious); (b) two of the five abstinence trials enrolled only people with non-daily use (low-frequency subgroup OR 1.24, 0.34-4.48, I2 74%); (c) the trials' own abstinence definitions differ in detail (e.g. Anderson 2015 counted at least two negative urines in weeks 11-12 as success, per Table 1), so 'urine-verified abstinence in the final two weeks' is the review's harmonised label; (d) for retention, a subgroup of two trials with more than 12 weeks of treatment (both methylphenidate, one in incarcerated men with ADHD) gave OR 2.45 (1.14-5.25), subgroup-difference p = 0.05, which the authors treat as hypothesis-generating; (e) a 151-participant bupropion trial (Elkashef 2008) entered neither analysis, excluded from retention for a stated sample overlap with Anderson 2015 that the review does not explain.

anchors.locator: Methods > Data sources; Inclusion and exclusion criteria; Data synthesis, 1st-3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Five databases searched from inception to August 2016 plus reference lists and ClinicalTrials.gov. Eligible: RCTs comparing any psychostimulant with placebo in people aged 14 or over with DSM amphetamine or methamphetamine use disorder (DSM-IV abuse or dependence included); withdrawal trials excluded. Primary outcomes: abstinence (proportion with substance-free urines, longest substance-free period used) and retention (proportion remaining in treatment at end of trial); secondary: serious adverse events. Random-effects inverse-variance odds ratios in RevMan 5.3; intention to treat with number randomized as denominator; I2 > 40% taken as substantial.

anchors.locator: Abstract (Results); Results > Description of studies, 1st-4th paragraphs; Table 1
anchors.extracted: 17 parallel-group placebo-controlled RCTs, 1387 participants: modafinil 3, bupropion 6, methylphenidate 6, dexamphetamine or dextroamphetamine 2; one adolescent trial, others adults 18-65; most DSM-IV methamphetamine dependence. In Anderson 2012 the 200 mg and 400 mg modafinil arms were combined against placebo.

anchors.locator: Results > Meta-analyses: efficacy of psychostimulants for abstinence, 1st-2nd paragraphs; Fig. 4a legend
anchors.extracted: Five of 17 trials pooled for abstinence (Anderson 2015, Heinzerling 2014 and Shoptaw 2008 for bupropion; Heinzerling 2010 and Anderson 2012 for modafinil), all in methamphetamine dependence (regular or low-frequency use), outcome 'terminal abstinence' = methamphetamine-free urines in the final 2 weeks. Other trials excluded because outcomes were reported inconsistently or lacked participant-level abstinence counts. 642 participants (353 medication, 289 placebo); pooled OR 0.97 (95% CI 0.65-1.45), p = 0.87; I2 2% (chi-square 4.08, df 4, p = 0.40).

anchors.locator: Discussion > Table 2 (GRADE evidence profile) and Table 3 (Summary of findings), with footnotes a-f
anchors.extracted: Abstinence (final 2 weeks of treatment, urinalysis): 70/353 (19.8%) vs 62/289 (21.5%); OR 0.97 (0.65-1.45); placebo risk 215 per 1,000; 5 fewer per 1,000 (64 fewer to 69 more); very low certainty (risk of bias very serious, inconsistency serious, indirectness serious, imprecision very serious). Retention (end of trial, follow-up 8-24 weeks): 332/626 (53.0%) vs 268/558 (48.0%); OR 1.20 (0.91-1.58); placebo risk 480 per 1,000; 46 more per 1,000 (23 fewer to 113 more); very low certainty.

anchors.locator: Results > Subgroup analyses (abstinence), 1st-2nd paragraphs; Fig. 4b-c legends
anchors.extracted: By drug: modafinil OR 0.86 (0.46-1.61), I2 0%; bupropion OR 1.12 (0.54-2.33), I2 47%; test for subgroup differences chi-square 0.29, df 1, p = 0.59. By use frequency: people with non-daily use (2 trials) OR 1.24 (0.34-4.48), I2 74%; unspecified frequency OR 0.92 (0.54-1.54); subgroup difference p = 0.67. Subgroups by age, diagnosis and duration not possible with five trials.

anchors.locator: Results > Meta-analyses: efficacy of psychostimulants for retention in treatment; Subgroup analyses (retention), 1st-3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: 14 trials pooled for retention (completion of the study); Tiihonen 2007 and the adolescent trial excluded for missing dropout data, Elkashef 2008 excluded for a stated sample overlap with Anderson 2015. 1184 participants (626 medication, 558 placebo); OR 1.20 (0.91-1.58); I2 15% (chi-square 15.34, df 13, p = 0.29). By drug (four subgroups) no significant effect, subgroup difference chi-square 2.31, df 3, p = 0.51; dexamphetamine (2 trials) OR 2.50 (0.80-7.87). Amphetamine vs methamphetamine use disorder: OR 1.54 (0.48-4.99) vs 1.11 (0.86-1.44).

anchors.locator: Results > Subgroup analyses (retention), last paragraph; Discussion, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Treatment longer than 12 weeks (two trials, Konstenius 2014 and Miles 2013, both methylphenidate): OR 2.45 (1.14-5.25), p = 0.02; test for subgroup differences chi-square 3.93, df 1, p = 0.05, I2 74.5%. Authors: based on two studies, cannot be generalised; retention in the prison sample may reflect expectations about parole.

anchors.locator: Table 1 (summary of substance-use outcomes, by trial)
anchors.extracted: Trials outside the abstinence pooling reported mixed urine results as summarised by the review: methylphenidate fewer positive urines in Tiihonen 2007 (OR 0.42, 0.24-0.72), Ling 2014 (OR 0.18 at week 14, p = 0.025), Rezaei 2015 (p = 0.03) and Konstenius 2014 (p = 0.047), no difference in Konstenius 2010 and Miles 2013; dexamphetamine no between-group difference (Galloway 2011, Longo 2009); the adolescent bupropion trial favoured placebo (5.0 vs 8.9 negative urines, p = 0.043). Within the pooled set, Anderson 2015 14/100 vs 20/104 and Heinzerling 2014 12/41 vs 6/43.

anchors.locator: Results > Risk of bias assessment, 1st-3rd paragraphs; Discussion, 4th paragraph; Strengths and limitations
anchors.extracted: Random sequence generation adequately reported in under half of trials; over 75% (GRADE footnote: 80%) did not report allocation concealment; all trials unclear or high risk for outcome-assessor blinding; most trials lost over 50% of participants; 47% of trials had 30 or fewer per arm. Only published data used; no additional data sought from investigators. Overall quality of evidence very low.

key_findings.correction: 17 trials and 1251 unique citations are in Results > Description of studies; the 1387 total is printed in the Abstract (Results) and the Table 1 rows sum to it (recomputed). Drug counts match the list in Description of studies, 4th paragraph.

Recomputed: 19.8% and 21.5%; GRADE-style 5 fewer per 1,000 (64 fewer to 69 more) from the pooled OR and the 215 per 1,000 placebo risk; editors' crude risk difference -1.6 points (-7.9 to 4.7) reproduces.
Recomputed: 53.0% and 48.0%; 46 more per 1,000 (23 fewer to 113 more); editors' crude risk difference 5.0 points (-0.7 to 10.7) reproduces.

All values as printed in Table 1. For Konstenius 2014 the table labels the per-group values 'MD = 23%' and 'MD = 16%' while its abbreviation list defines MD as mean difference; reading them as group proportions of negative urines, as the card does, is the only sensible reading but is an interpretation of a mislabelled cell.

The text calls these counts 'dropouts' in the serious-adverse-event paragraph (8 + 11 + 7 = 26 vs 11), without saying they were caused by serious events; under the review's definition (an event causing hospitalisation or dropout) they are its serious-event counts, so the card's reading is fair, but 'dropouts counted under the review's serious-adverse-event definition' is closer to the text.

reporting_issues.note: Recounted: Table 1 lists ten trials with study length over 12 weeks (eight of them in the retention analysis). One nuance: Table 1's column is 'study length', which may include post-treatment follow-up (e.g. Ling 2014's dosing runs to week 10 within a 14-week length; Elkashef 2008's schedule gives about 12 weeks of dosing within 18), so part of the discrepancy may be treatment versus study length; the clearest error is the citation of reference 25 (13 weeks) instead of 26 (24 weeks) for the 20-24-week trials. The conclusion (classification cannot be reproduced from the paper) stands.

Article side confirmed (Results > retention: Elkashef excluded for overlapping sample with reference 12; Table 1: 151 participants, 18 weeks, any frequency of use vs 204 participants, 12 weeks, non-daily use; Methods: the larger trial was kept when samples overlapped). Cross-reference confirmed from my reading of siefried_2020 (Table 4): Elkashef 2008 (n = 156) and Anderson 2015 (n = 204, use on fewer than 30 of the past 30 days) are listed as separate bupropion trials, and Table 4 even says Anderson 2015 'contradicts Elkashef 2008'. The card's replication-timeline entry on Siefried 2020 is also confirmed: 14 of Bhatt's 17 trials are in its reference list, Das 2010 and both Konstenius trials are absent, Ling 2014 is summarised there as showing no difference by urine (Bhatt Table 1: OR 0.18 at week 14), and Elkashef 2008 is given 156 participants (Bhatt: 151).
The same Discussion paragraph also says heterogeneity was relatively low for both outcomes, which contradicts its 'little to no overlap' sentence.
The abstract does hedge the sentence with 'based on qualitative reports from trials'; the card's point (no incidence was calculated, counts lack denominators) stands.
Recounted after the stated exclusions (Elkashef 2008, Tiihonen 2007, Heinzerling 2013): modafinil 3, bupropion 4, methylphenidate 5, dexamphetamine 2 = 14; 'two to six' cannot be right.

risk_of_bias.note: Agree with the overall 'low confidence' and with most item judgments, but items 11 and 12 use 'partial yes', which AMSTAR 2 does not offer for those items (partial yes exists only for items 2, 4, 7, 8 and 9; items 11 and 12 are yes / no / no meta-analysis). On AMSTAR 2's criteria item 11 would be 'yes' (rationale for pooling psychostimulants as a class is given in the Background, random-effects inverse-variance pooling, heterogeneity investigated with prespecified subgroups); if the editors instead treat the unexplained exclusion of Elkashef 2008 as an inappropriate method, item 11 becomes 'no', a second critical flaw, and the overall rating falls to critically low. Item 12 would be 'yes' (sensitivity analyses removing trials at high risk for selective reporting and incomplete outcome data were run, though only described as not changing the results). Item 3 'no' is defensible on a strict reading (no rationale given for restricting to RCTs). Item 4's note that the search ended within 3 months of submission could not be checked: the article-notes panel with the submission date is not in the saved text. Item 7 'no' (no list of excluded full texts) is the critical flaw and is correct.

interpretation_gap.note: The three gaps the card names are all in the text and correctly described. I would rate the gap 'substantial' rather than 'minor': the abstract and Conclusions state that psychostimulants as a class had no effect on sustained abstinence, while the abstinence analysis contained only bupropion and modafinil (no methylphenidate or dexamphetamine trial, i.e. 8 of the 17 trials' drugs untested on that outcome, four methylphenidate trials reporting fewer positive urines in Table 1), and 'no effect' is stated for intervals that allow roughly 6 points of benefit or harm (OR 0.65-1.45). The Discussion's body text is precise (it limits the null abstinence finding to modafinil and bupropion), so the gap is between the body and the abstract and conclusions. Senior-author call.

missed: Card field outcomes.multiplicity_correction says the six subgroup tests produced 16 subgroup estimates; recounted from Results, they produced 14 (abstinence by drug 2 and by frequency 2; retention by diagnosis 2, by drug 4, by frequency 2, by duration 2). Minor correction to the card text.
